message.content:
You are searching the "memos" Go codebase at /bench/repo. Answer with precise file paths and line numbers. Search breadth: very thorough.

Q1 (h10): Among functions/methods declared under an internal/ directory (check if the repo has internal/ — e.g. internal/util, internal/base, internal/profile or similar; run `ls` to see), which single function or method has the highest inbound-call count (fan-in) from the rest of the codebase? Method: list exported functions in internal/ packages, then grep the whole repo for call sites of each (e.g. util.GenUUID, util.ValidateEmail, base.X). Count approximate callers (non-test and total). Report the winner with path of declaration and approximate caller count, plus the runner-up for comparison.

Q2 (h11): The data layer is the store/ package with persistent entity types (structs like Memo, User, Resource/Attachment, Activity, IdentityProvider, Webhook, Reaction, MemoRelation, UserSetting, WorkspaceSetting...). Determine, for each entity type, how many distinct Go packages OUTSIDE the store layer (i.e. not under store/) reference the type (grep for 'store.Memo', 'store.User', '\*store.Memo' etc., group hits by package directory). Rank the top two entity types by number of distinct outside packages, with rough package counts and example citations.

Return raw findings with citations and your counting method.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

## Q1 — Highest fan-in function declared under `internal/`

**Method:** enumerated every exported `func`/method in each `internal/*` package (`grep "^func "` per dir, excluding `_test.go`), then grepped the whole repo for `<pkg>.<Name>(` call sites, bucketed by declaring-package-internal vs. external, and by test vs. non-test.

Aggregate frequency table (call sites outside the declaring package):

```
 28  util.GenUUID(
 12  scheduler.New(          <- all 12 are inside internal/scheduler's own tests + doc.go comments
  7  filter.DefaultEngine(
  6  filter.AppendConditions(
  5  util.ConvertStringToInt32(   /  scheduler.WithMiddleware(  /  s3.NewClient(
  4  version.IsVersionGreaterThan(  /  markdown.NewService(  /  filter.DefaultAttachmentEngine(
  3  webhook.ValidateURL(  /  webhook.ValidateSigningSecret(  /  version.GetCurrentVersion(
```

### Winner: `util.GenUUID`
Declared at `/bench/repo/internal/util/util.go:40`

- **28 total call sites**, in **4 distinct packages**, **0 of them inside `internal/`** (pure external fan-in).
- **7 non-test call sites** across 6 files:
  - `/bench/repo/server/auth/token.go:194`
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_session.go:26` and `:135`
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service_storage.go:209`
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go:154`
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sso_username.go:15`
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_access_tokens.go:84`
- **21 test call sites**: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/auth_test.go` (19 sites, e.g. `:122`, `:151`, `:469-470`, `:611-615`, `:660`), `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/authz_test.go:65`, `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go:576`.

### Runner-up: `filter.DefaultEngine`
Declared at `/bench/repo/internal/filter/engine.go:111`

- **7 call sites, all non-test**, in **4 distinct packages** — broader package spread than GenUUID's non-test spread, but a third of the raw count:
  - `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go:341`
  - `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo.go:57`, `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo_relation.go:81`
  - `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/memo.go:54`, `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/memo_relation.go:83`
  - `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/memo.go:65`, `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/memo_relation.go:74`

Third place is `filter.AppendConditions` (`/bench/repo/internal/filter/helpers.go:9`, 6 sites, all in the three `store/db/*` driver packages).

Note on `scheduler.New` (`/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:54`): 12 raw matches, but they are all in `internal/scheduler/example_test.go`, `integration_test.go`, and comment lines in `doc.go` — zero real production callers, so it is excluded from the ranking.

Also worth noting: `internal/base` (`/bench/repo/internal/base/resource_name.go:6`) exports no functions at all — only the `UIDMatcher` regexp var (8 references repo-wide).

## Q2 — Entity types by number of distinct non-store packages referencing them

**Method:** listed all `type X struct` declarations in `/bench/repo/store/*.go`; for each entity name grepped `(\*|\[\]|\(|^|[^A-Za-z0-9_.])store\.<Name>\b` repo-wide (the char-class prefix + `\b` avoids matching `store.UserSetting` when counting `store.User`), then filtered out `store/**` (which excludes the `store/db/{sqlite,postgres,mysql}` drivers and `store/test`) and `proto/gen/**` (the generated `.pb.go` files contain literal descriptor strings like `.memos.store.MemoPayload`, which are false positives), then `dirname | sort -u` to group by package.

Full ranking (distinct outside packages / raw hit count):

| Entity | outside pkgs | hits | packages |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`store.User`** | **7** (6 non-test) | 93 | api/v1, fileserver, auth, notification, rss, frontend, api/v1/test |
| **`store.Memo`** | **6** (5 non-test) | 64 | api/v1, notification, rss, frontend, runner/memopayload, api/v1/test |
| `store.Attachment` | 4 (3 non-test) | 43 | api/v1, fileserver, rss, api/v1/test |
| `store.MemoRelation` | 3 | 9 | api/v1, rss, api/v1/test |
| `store.Inbox` | 3 | 13 | api/v1, notification, api/v1/test |
| `store.MemoShare` | 3 | 10 | api/v1, fileserver, api/v1/test |
| `store.Reaction` | 2 | 14 | api/v1, api/v1/test |
| `store.UserIdentity` | 2 | 9 | api/v1, api/v1/test |
| `store.IdentityProvider`, `store.UserSetting`, `store.InstanceSetting` | 0 | 0 | referenced **only** inside `store/` (the three DB drivers); the API layer works with the `storepb` proto types instead |

### #1 — `store.User` (declared `/bench/repo/store/user.go:29`)
7 distinct outside packages, 93 hits. Per-package: `server/router/api/v1` 57, `server/router/fileserver` 12, `server/router/api/v1/test` 8, `server/auth` 7, `server/notification` 5, `server/router/rss` 3, `server/router/frontend` 1.

Citations:
- `/bench/repo/server/auth/context.go:55` — `func SetUserInContext(ctx context.Context, user *store.User, accessToken string) context.Context`
- `/bench/repo/server/auth/authenticator.go:61`
- `/bench/repo/server/notification/email.go:136`
- `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:162`
- `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:708`
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_session.go:24`, `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_settings.go:229`

### #2 — `store.Memo` (declared `/bench/repo/store/memo.go:35`)
6 distinct outside packages, 64 hits. Per-package: `server/router/api/v1` 38, `server/router/api/v1/test` 10, `server/notification` 10, `server/router/rss` 3, `server/router/frontend` 2, `server/runner/memopayload` 1.

Citations:
- `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74` — `func RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error`
- `/bench/repo/server/notification/email.go:136`
- `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:162`
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:23` — `convertMemoFromStore(ctx, memo *store.Memo, reactions []*store.Reaction, attachments []*store.Attachment, ...)`
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go:27`, `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39`

The distinguishing package for `User` vs `Memo` is `server/auth`, which threads `*store.User` through the auth context but never touches `store.Memo`; `server/runner/memopayload` is the reverse (Memo only). `server/router/fileserver` references `User` and `Attachment` heavily but not `Memo`.

Caveat: entity types you listed as `Resource`, `Activity`, `Webhook`, `WorkspaceSetting`, and `Shortcut` do not exist as store structs in this revision — `Resource` was renamed to `Attachment` (`/bench/repo/store/attachment.go:16`), workspace settings became `InstanceSetting` (`/bench/repo/store/instance_setting.go:14`), and webhooks/shortcuts are now stored as proto payloads inside user settings (see `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:288`, `convertUserWebhookFromUserSetting(webhook *storepb.WebhooksUserSetting_Webhook, ...)`).
